name: Cadet Blue
lede: Cadet Blue is a muted greenish blue named for the grey-blue of cadet uniforms; it entered web color lists as one of the 140 X11 names.

sections.title: A uniform color
sections.body: St Clair glosses cadet blue as a grey-greenish blue taken from military uniforms [1]. Paterson defines it as a bluish grey or a strong blue, and notes the variant *cadet grey* [2]. The books therefore disagree on how blue it is: one says grey, another says a strong blue [1][2]. The swatch is a greyed teal, between [[steel-blue]] and [[teal]], and close in family to [[cadet-grey]] [3].

sections.title: The web name
sections.body: Paterson lists `CadetBlue` as one of the 140 colors of the X11 color set, with the hex code #5F9EA0 [2]. That is the swatch shown here, which is why the word is better known on screens than in dye or paint catalogues [2][3]. The same dictionary files it in its table of blues [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Cadet Blue is a rare color in painting: 36 of 23,781 paintings in the ColorHub archive contain it, as photographed [3]. It is most common in the 1500s, and Juan de Flandes has it in 3 of his 13 paintings, far above the rate for the archive [3]. Among the larger patches is Odilon Redon's *Village by the Sea in Brittany* of 1880 [3]. A search of printed books shows the phrase *cadet blue* rising from the 1880s and peaking around 1921 [4].
